GOVERNING PRODUCT DIRECTION (corrected 2026-09-04; UNBLOCKED). intercom-go is a per-workspace Go backend brokering a GitHub Copilot agent session between two co-equal operator surfaces: a local Bubble Tea TUI and a remote SPA reached over a Microsoft Dev Tunnel. CORRECTIONS APPLIED to this entry's original text: (1) the remote client is an SPA, NOT iOS -- the iOS wording is stale; SPA framework choice is deliberately OUT OF SCOPE; (2) the agent boundary is the OFFICIAL GitHub Copilot SDK for Go (github.com/github/copilot-sdk/go, pinned v1.0.11 = commit a550258d5c37bd662197536992a23d633bfe5804), NOT coder/acp-go-sdk -- intercom-go implements no ACP broker, no ACP wire protocol, and no direct headless-Copilot-CLI lifecycle. That the SDK internally manages a Copilot CLI server over JSON-RPC is an SDK IMPLEMENTATION DETAIL (its codec is under internal/ and unimportable by hosts); (3) the three load-bearing conflicts recorded here are RESOLVED: durability -- the backend projection is a CACHE and the SDK runtime is the durable event source via GetEvents/ResumeSession, bridged by the D4a minimal session pointer (a pointer, not a store; D7 full persistence remains deferred); operator surface in the persistence schema -- moot, Slack is retired so slack_ts/thread_ts/channel_id vanish with it; lifecycle ownership -- settled as one isolated process per workspace, orchestrated by autoharness, one allocated HTTP/WS port (the second ACP port is gone). (4) The AgentDriver-vs-OperatorGateway distinction recorded here is PRESERVED and now realised: the SDK adapter is the agent-facing side, and the OperatorGateway (event envelopes, hydration/reconnect, first-responder arbitration, WebSocket backpressure) is the operator-facing side. DEFERRED SCOPE EXPANSION: internal/pathsafe/pathsafe.go's checkSymlinkEscape ancestor-existence probe uses os.Stat (which follows symlinks) when walking up from a resolved path to find the nearest existing ancestor. The function's own doc comment documents the dangling-symlink acceptance as a known limitation ONLY for the FINAL path component (GO-14). Multi-model adversarial review (2026-09-06, shipment 010-S) found this same os.Stat-follows-symlinks mechanism also applies to any INTERMEDIATE ancestor: if an intermediate component is a symlink whose target does not yet exist (dangling), os.Stat on that ancestor errors, the walk treats it as absent and walks PAST it without ever re-resolving/re-checking that symlinks own target for containment -- e.g. root/danglinglink pointing outside the workspace to a not-yet-existing target; Resolve(danglinglink/new-file.txt) walks past danglinglink, and a later write once the external target is created lands outside the workspace. Out of scope per P-021 C1: this is pre-existing containment-control logic from a prior shipment (005-S), not modified by shipment 010-S's 20 authorized units (010-S's 011.006-T only added doc comments/tests for a DIFFERENT documented-unreachable branch in the same function, the filesystem-root fallback -- not this ancestor-walk mechanism). A related but distinct, already-resolved task is 010.004-T (GO-14 dangling-symlink test for the FINAL component only). Requires deliberation: true (Stage should assess severity/priority and schedule a Constitution-VIII-compliant containment-logic fix with a mandatory red-phase negative test, or use os.Lstat/explicit os.ModeSymlink detection during the ancestor walk).
